meta.method: WebSearch + WebFetch, plus curl/pdftotext and SheetJS (in scratchpad) where WebFetch could not render a page or parse a PDF/XLS. confirmed:true only where the figure was read on the cited page or document itself (including text extracted locally from the downloaded file). Search-engine snippet summaries are recorded as confirmed:false. Nothing estimated; gaps recorded as 'not found'. About 45 fetches/searches.

hotel_early_late.item: Premier Inn (UK) standard check-in time and early check-in hour
hotel_early_late.figure: Standard check-in 3pm; paid early check-in from 11am ('For an additional fee*'); subject to availability and not at all hotels
hotel_early_late.note: Read in the page's FAQ structured data: 'Our standard check-in time is 3pm. For an additional fee*, you can start your stay sooner with early check-in from 11am.' The page's extras config also says 'Start your stay from 11am instead of the usual 3pm'.
'Checkout is by 12 noon on your departure date.'

hotel_early_late.figure: Check out at 2pm instead of 12pm (paid extra); cannot be booked within a set number of hours of departure
hotel_early_late.note: Read in the site's booking-extras configuration strings embedded in the page (extra code HSCOU2: 'Check out at 2pm instead of 12pm'). Price not shown on the page.

The search summary attributed '£10 ... UK and Channel Islands only; Republic of Ireland is charged at €10' to Premier Inn's FAQ, but the footnote text with the price was not present in the HTML I downloaded (the asterisk footnote renders client-side). Airport-hotel variants (early from 10am for £10; late to 4pm for £20) appear only in third-party summaries; not confirmed.

Booking terms D1: 'You can check in after 3pm on the scheduled date of arrival unless you purchase an early check-in Extra...'; D2: 'You must check-out before midday on the scheduled date of departure unless you purchase a l[ate check-out Extra]'.

hotel_early_late.item: Travelodge (UK) early check-in and late check-out extras
hotel_early_late.figure: Early check-in from 12 noon (normally 3pm); late check-out up until 2pm (normally 12 noon); 'Charges apply'; at selected hotels, subject to availability
hotel_early_late.note: Also on the FAQ page (https://www.travelodge.co.uk/about/frequently-asked-questions/): 'pre-paid early check-in service from 12 noon ... at an additional cost' and 'prepaid late check-out service up to 2pm'. Price not stated on either page.

hotel_early_late.item: Travelodge (UK) early check-in / late check-out price
hotel_early_late.note: Only from search summaries quoting third-party sites ('For just £10 per service'). Travelodge's own pages say only 'Charges apply'. Price shown at booking is not visible without a booking session.

hotel_early_late.item: Maldron Hotel Kevin Street (Dublin) times and late check-out fee
hotel_early_late.figure: Check-in from 3.00pm; check-out 11.00am; late check-out €10 per hour until 3.00pm; early check-in only guaranteed by booking the previous night
hotel_early_late.note: 'It may be possible to check-out later than 11.00am with a €10 charge per hour until 3.00pm.' Maldron sets these per hotel; no chain-wide policy found.

hotel_early_late.item: Maldron Hotel Belfast City times and fees
hotel_early_late.figure: Check-in from 3pm; check-out 11.00am; early check-in £20 per hour; late check-out £20 per hour, max 2 hours
hotel_early_late.note: Northern Ireland property, priced in sterling.

hotel_early_late.item: Marriott Bonvoy late check-out (Platinum Elite and above)
hotel_early_late.figure: 4 p.m. local time; guaranteed except at resort and convention hotels, Design Hotels and StudioRes (availability-based); Apartments by Marriott Bonvoy guarantee 2 p.m.; vacation clubs excluded
hotel_early_late.note: Read verbatim in the downloaded terms: 'v. 4 p.m. Late Checkout. Platinum Elite Members and above may check out as late as 4 p.m. local time ... This benefit is guaranteed at all Participating Properties, except at resort and convention hotels, Design Hotels, and StudioRes, where it is based upon availability.' Gold: 'iii. 2 p.m. Late Checkout. This benefit is based on availability.' Silver: 'Priority Late Checkout. Based on availability.' Marriott does not publish a chain-wide standard check-in/out hour (set per property). View from the Wing reported the Japanese terms cut the Platinum guarantee to 2pm; the English terms I read still say 4 p.m.

hotel_early_late.figure: Diamond Reserve (new 2026 tier): guaranteed 4:00 p.m., automatic; other tiers: on request, subject to availability
hotel_early_late.note: Diamond Reserve 4pm read on this page. The 'subject to availability' wording for Gold/Diamond is from search summaries of Hilton's terms (hilton.com terms page returned 403); not read on Hilton's own page. Secondary source.

hotel_early_late.figure: $40 (Hampton, Hilton Garden Inn, Home2 etc.), $50 (DoubleTree, Embassy Suites etc.), $60 (Conrad, Waldorf Astoria, Hilton, Curio etc.); bookable up to 72 hours ahead; launch 'some point in 2026'
hotel_early_late.note: Read on the article; the article itself notes the check-out time granted was not specified. Not verified on hilton.com.

hotel_early_late.figure: Up to 2pm on request, subject to hotel availability, all members, all IHG brands
hotel_early_late.note: IHG terms page returned 403 to both WebFetch and curl; figure is from the search-engine summary of that page. No IHG paid early/late fee schedule found.

hotel_early_late.item: World of Hyatt Globalist late check-out
hotel_early_late.figure: Guaranteed 4 p.m. on request; subject to availability at casino hotels, resorts and Destination Residences; not offered at Hyatt Vacation Club / vacation ownership
hotel_early_late.note: Read on NerdWallet. Hyatt's own terms page is JavaScript-rendered and could not be read. No Hyatt paid early/late fee schedule found.

hotel_early_late.item: Standard check-in/check-out hours at Marriott, Hilton, IHG, Hyatt
hotel_early_late.note: None of the four US chains publishes a chain-wide hour that I could read; each property sets its own. Only UK/Irish chains (Premier Inn 3pm/12 noon, Travelodge 3pm/midday, Maldron 3pm/11am) publish them.

hotel_early_late.item: Industry survey: share of hotels charging for early check-in / late check-out and typical amount
hotel_early_late.note: Search summaries cited '63% allow early check-in free / 37% charge', '$20-$50 average (TravelPulse)', and '68% allow early check-in (Hotel News Resource)', but none traced to a primary survey with methodology; no NerdWallet or Skift study on this was found. Do not use.

architect_fee.item: RAIC fee guideline: Category 7 'Custom Residence' (Appendix D lists 'House - Custom Residence 7'), new construction, fee net of engineering
architect_fee.figure: Under $500,000: to be negotiated, minimum base fee 13.50%. $500k-<$1M: simple 11.50%, average 14.25%, complex 17.00%. $1M-<$2M: simple 10.50%, average 13.25%, complex 16.00%. $2M-<$5M: 9.75 / 12.63 / 15.50%
architect_fee.publisher: Royal Architectural Institute of Canada, 'A Guide to Determining Appropriate Fees for the Services of an Architect' (endorsed by MAA, OAA, AAPPQ, OAQ, AANB, AAPEI, NSAA, NLAA, NWTAA)
architect_fee.note: Read from chart 1.1.4 (page 11) of the PDF text. The copy is hosted by an architecture firm, not raic.ca. Fees 'must be adjusted based on fee adjustment factors'. The 2009 edition is the one found; a newer edition may exist.

architect_fee.item: RAIC Category 7 including basic engineering (structural, mechanical, electrical)
RIBA (UK) fee method and stage split
architect_fee.figure: No percentage given for a new house. Stage split: stages 0-3 = 35% of fee; stage 4 = 35%; stages 5-6 = 30%. Many architects accept a variance up to 10% of the construction budget before adjusting a percentage fee
architect_fee.note: RIBA's homeowner page names percentage, lump-sum and time-charge methods but publishes no percentage. No RIBA fee survey figure was found.

architect_fee.figure: New house: 10.5% at £100k budget, 9.5% at £200k, 9% at £500k, 8.5% at £1m
architect_fee.note: From search summary only; not fetched. A single firm's figures, not a RIBA survey.
No AIA-published fee percentage for houses found. (Background, not verified this session: the AIA has not published fee schedules since antitrust consent decrees in the 1970s-1990s.)

architect_fee.figure: Around 5% for new construction jobs; 8%-15% for most projects; national average $6,625 (typical $2,189-$11,550)
architect_fee.note: Read on the page. A consumer cost guide, not a professional-body figure.
No RIAI fee percentage found. Irish secondary sites (buildtech.ie, beforeyoubuild.ie) quote 8-12% or 10-15% for new homes; not fetched, not confirmed.

construction_delay.item: US average months, start to completion, single-family (1-unit) buildings, permit-issuing places
construction_delay.publisher: US Census Bureau, Survey of Construction
construction_delay.note: Parsed from the downloaded XLS. This file has not been updated past 2022; later years come from the NAHB analyses below.

construction_delay.figure: 8.8 months total = 1.4 months authorization to start + 7.4 months start to completion. Permit-to-completion by type: built for sale 7.4, hired contractor 11.7, built for rent 12.4, owner-built 14.3 months. About 1.6 months longer than 2015
construction_delay.publisher: NAHB Eye on Housing, from Census Survey of Construction

construction_delay.note: From search summary of the 2024 and 2023 posts; not fetched.

construction_delay.item: Delay attributable to labor shortage (NAHB/HBI/University of Denver study)
construction_delay.figure: Unweighted average increase in construction time 1.98 months
construction_delay.publisher: NAHB / Home Builders Institute / University of Denver
construction_delay.note: Read on the press release; it does not give the share of builders reporting delays or sample size.

construction_delay.item: Share of single-family projects finishing late, and average overrun against the contracted schedule
construction_delay.note: No US, UK (NHBC, Glenigan, Barbour ABI) or other published measure of the share of new houses finishing behind their own schedule was found. Census measures elapsed time, not slippage against plan; the gap between built-for-sale and owner/contractor-built durations is the nearest published proxy.

easements.item: How often a rural US/UK lot needs an access or utility easement
easements.note: No statistic found on the share of private rural parcels needing or lacking an access/utility easement. Only landlocked public land acreage (16.43 million acres in 22 states, 2018) appeared, which is not about private lots.

HM Land Registry fee to register the grant of an easement
easements.figure: £40 fixed fee (£20 via portal or Business Gateway), under 'applications not otherwise referred to'

easements.item: US law-firm price, preparing or reviewing an easement
easements.note: One firm's fee schedule; county recording fee is separate. A search summary quoted a general '$100-$5,000' range (ContractsCounsel); not fetched.

easements.item: ALTA owner's policy: access is a covered risk
easements.figure: Covered Risk 4: 'No right of access to and from the Land.' (same in 2006 and 2021 ALTA Owner's Policy)
easements.publisher: American Land Title Association, Owner's Policy comparison chart
easements.note: Read from extracted PDF text. Recorded easements are normally listed as Schedule B exceptions (not covered) — that point is from search summaries (homeclosing101.org, Nolo), not confirmed.

easements.item: ALTA Homeowner's Policy access and easement-encroachment coverage
easements.figure: Insures 'actual vehicular and pedestrian access to and from the Land, based on a legal right' (standard owner's policy: 'a right of access'); also covers forced removal of structures encroaching onto easements or setback lines

empty_legs.item: Count of empty-leg listings per day, or how often a route gets one
empty_legs.note: No operator or broker (XO, Victor, Flexjet, BLADE) publishes daily listing counts or per-route frequency that I found. Victor's 'The truth about empty legs' returned 403.

empty_legs.item: Share of the private-jet charter fleet flying empty (XO estimate)
empty_legs.figure: 30 to 50 percent of the private jet charter fleet often flies empty
empty_legs.note: A broker's estimate quoted in a trade article, not a measured statistic. Same article quotes Wingly: '10 million seats fly without passengers in Europe alone every year'.

A search summary claimed '40% of all business aviation flights in Europe operate as empty repositioning legs according to EBAA', but no EBAA or WINGX page with the figure was found or read. Do not use.

illegal_tint_share.item: Police or government survey of the share of cars with tint darker than the legal limit
illegal_tint_share.note: None found for NHTSA, DVSA, a US state or Australia. NHTSA's March 1991 'Report to Congress on Tinting of Motor Vehicle Windows' appears in NHTSA interpretations but its prevalence data was not located. The DC Police Complaints Board report (2013-11-21) was read: it covers complaints about tint enforcement (e.g. 97% of tint-related complaints share a characteristic) but gives no prevalence figure.

illegal_tint_share.figure: Windscreen at least 75% light transmission; front side windows at least 70% (vehicles first used on or after 1 April 1985); police or DVSA measure with light meters
illegal_tint_share.note: From the search summary of the GOV.UK page; not fetched.

actra_ipa.item: IPA 2025-2027 B501: use-payment options chosen at the time of production
actra_ipa.figure: (a) All Uses Prepayment, worldwide incl. New Media, 4 years from first release in any Residual Market: 135% of Net Fees (theatrical) / 110% (TV and other). (b) Conventional Use Prepayment, excl. New Media, 4 years: 130% theatrical / 105% TV. (c) Advance Option, non-refundable advance against DGR participation: 100% of Net Fees -> 3.6% of DGR; 75% -> 4.6%; 50% -> 5.6%; 25% -> 6.6%
actra_ipa.publisher: ACTRA / CMPA / AQPM, Independent Production Agreement, 26 January 2025 - 31 December 2027
actra_ipa.note: Read from extracted text, pp. 115-116. Wording: 'The Producer shall declare and specify the prepayment in the individual contract of the Performer. The prepayment must be paid to Performers at the time of production.' Advance option: 'The Producer may pay, at the time of production, one of the following percentages of Net Fees as a non-refundable advance ("Advance") against the following Use fees ... based on Performer participation in DGR'. Same options in the 2019-2021 IPA (Art. B501).

actra_ipa.item: B504 Participation in Gross after prepayment
actra_ipa.figure: 3.6% of DGR in aggregate to performers (5% for CIPIP; 8% for Option 1 New Media productions budgeted at $111,735/minute or less), only on revenue after the 4-year prepaid period
actra_ipa.note: Verbatim: 'If the Producer elects to make a prepayment as set out in Article B501(a) or (b) or D111(a) or (b), the Performers shall be paid Use fees in the aggregate in the amount of 3.6% of the DGR ... except that revenues earned by the Production within the first four (4) year period of prepaid Use shall not entitle the Performer to receive any such payments on such revenues'. B504(b): after a conventional prepayment, New Media exploitation pays 3.6% of DGR 'from the date of first exploitation in the New Media Use'. The 2019-2021 IPA had a $10,000/minute threshold in place of $111,735.

actra_ipa.figure: No DGR use fees paid until the Aggregate Advance is recouped from DGR; an individual's advance is capped at 50% of Gross Fees; credit per performer is capped at days of principal photography x 12 x the Principal Actor daily minimum (2025-2027; the 2019-2021 IPA used x 20)
actra_ipa.note: B505: 'Performers shall be paid, as Use fees, an aggregate amount equal to the applicable percentage of DGR, provided that no amounts shall be paid until such time as the Aggregate Advance ... is recouped from the DGR.' The x20 -> x12 change was read by comparing the two editions (2019-2021 copy: https://www.actratoronto.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/IPA-2019-2021-16.pdf).

actra_ipa.figure: All monies from distribution, first dollar, no deductions; excludes merchandising, novelization and sequel rights; includes presales but not distribution advances; EST and disc sales deemed 20% of wholesale (10% if at or under about $30 per unit)
actra_ipa.note: 'calculated before or simultaneously with any other gross participants from first dollar, without deductions of expenses of any kind.' The deemed-DGR detail for EST/discs was read in the 2019-2021 text.

actra_ipa.item: B511 When DGR use fees are paid
actra_ipa.figure: Reports with payment due to ACTRA PRS at least semi-annually for the first 2 years after the first report, then annually; first report due 60 days after the end of the first reporting period, which starts on delivery to the Distributor; late payment interest at prime + 3%, calculated monthly
actra_ipa.note: Verbatim B511(c): 'The DGR shall be recognized when a contract for the sale or conveyance of any rights in a Production is made, but Use payments shall be payable only when the reports are due under Article B511(a).' Reports follow the producer's reporting frequency to government agencies/financiers if more frequent.

actra_ipa.item: B512 How the 3.6% pool is split among performers (relation to a performer's fee)
actra_ipa.figure: Units: 1 unit = minimum fee for the lowest-rated residual category for one day; each performer earns units according to Gross Fee paid, max 20 units; pool / total units = value per unit
actra_ipa.note: So the 3.6% is an aggregate for the whole cast, not 3.6% per performer; a performer's share is proportional to fee up to the 20-unit cap. 'Net Fees' (A427) means fees for days in front of the camera or behind the microphone, incl. blocking and ADR, with overtime, rehearsal and makeup on such days; it excludes meal penalties, travel, per diems, etc.

actra_ipa.figure: Prepayment period 4 years for features, free-TV movies and mini-series, direct-to-video and pay TV; 5 years for free-TV series, cable and New Media (BC agreement); after expiry, use fees are a percentage of DGR
actra_ipa.note: UBCP's page is about BC practice; the national IPA B501 gives 4 years for both prepayment options. Use the IPA text as primary.
